items.title: Cancelling a Shipped order returns 409 with the domain message
items.reason: This is the reported bug (cancel of a Shipped order returned 500); a domain rule violation must be a client error. Functional layer is the cheapest that exercises the endpoint, mediator pipeline and real persistence.

items.title: Cancelling a Paid order returns 409 with the domain message
items.reason: SetCancelledStatus rejects both Paid and Shipped; a separate case guards the Paid branch of the rule.

items.title: Shipping an order that is not Paid returns 409 with the domain message
items.reason: The bug covers ship as well as cancel (OrdersApi maps both); SetShippedStatus only allows Paid.

items.title: Shipping an already Shipped order returns 409
items.reason: Repeated ship with a new request id is a state transition that is not allowed.

items.title: Cancelling a nonexistent order returns 404
covers: Suggested fix: 404 when the order does not exist
items.reason: Nonexistent order must be distinguished from a rule violation; the existing test CancelNonExistentOrderFails asserts 500 and must change to 404.

items.title: Shipping a nonexistent order returns 404
covers: Suggested fix: 404 when the order does not exist
items.reason: Same as cancel, for the ship endpoint (existing ShipNonExistentOrderFails asserts 500 and must change).

items.title: Cancel with order number 0 returns 400 with the validation message
items.reason: Validator failures also surface as OrderingDomainException; they must map to 400, not to the 409 of a status rule. Boundary of NotEmpty on OrderNumber.

items.title: Ship with order number 0 returns 400 with the validation message
items.reason: Same mapping on the ship endpoint, which has its own validator.

items.title: Cancel with an empty request id still returns 400
items.reason: Regression guard: the new error mapping must not change the existing request-id check.

items.title: Ship with an empty request id still returns 400
items.reason: Regression guard on the ship endpoint.

items.title: Cancelling a Submitted order still returns 200 and sets status Cancelled
items.reason: The IdentifiedCommandHandler and endpoint were changed; the success path must be unaffected.

items.title: Shipping a Paid order still returns 200 and sets status Shipped
items.reason: Success path of ship must be unaffected by the new exception mapping.

items.title: A rejected cancel leaves the Shipped order unchanged
covers: Technical Notes: rule violation, not a server fault
items.reason: A 409 must not partially persist state; protects against the transaction committing despite the exception.

items.title: Retrying a rejected cancel with the same request id returns 409 again
covers: Deviations: transaction rolls back on rule violation, retry evaluated again
items.reason: The idempotency ClientRequest row now rolls back on a rule violation; a retry must be evaluated again, not reported as a duplicate success.

The plan must state that each test seeds its own order (or uses a fresh order id) so results do not depend on test order.

subject: test-automation
reason: All 14 cases have functional tests that follow the case's steps and assert the exact status codes, ProblemDetails detail strings, success status via GET, unchanged state after a rejected cancel, and re-evaluation on a retry with the same request id. Each test seeds its own order through the real domain model and DB, runs against the real endpoint with nothing mocked, and has no sleeps or shared mutable state.
